mechanism.occStep1Puzzle: B answers correctly without the pair that names its chain, and without doubling on m (removal singles it) — yet decoyQ proves it selects the NAMED chain among three. Filed open with hypotheses: (i) query-tip: the query weakly boosts its chain's signal and the readout amplifies small margins; (ii) the second hop (m,4+e)->e carries the load while the first hop is approximated by a query-prior the probe doesn't remove. Decisive test (not run): query-swap — keep pairs, swap QUERIES a<->c1: full-2hop predicts answers swap (e<->f1); readout predicts they stay.
mechanism.tension: C2-pass (doesn't need the naming pair) + FULL-2HOP (names any chain correctly) is the headline: B implements query-selected chain-following through a channel the occlusion battery cannot see — the first hop is not mediated by the (a,m) pair as a premise.

reading: FULL-2HOP — promote with honors. Pure 1-hop training compiled a query-conditional two-hop computation that answers TRUE and DECOY queries equally (0.45-0.52), follows relabeled chains, and dies only when the answer-source pair is removed. The stepping protocol (DECOMP-1) was never the missing piece because the compiled map already contains it. Next (proposed, not run): the query-swap decisive test, then cross-regime hops ONLY if query-swap confirms (else the probe battery needs redesign: the first hop's real channel is unidentified).
verdict: FULL-2HOP (C1 PASS, C2 PASS, C3 inverted-FAIL).
